title: Musicians who stayed clean now using heroin
summary: He notes that studio players who avoided drugs are now using it.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

Coming back from the dead.
Yeah.
There was a whole world of guys.
I didn't notice at first, but then I started to hear about it. Strange. Did it happen all the same period?
I never thought of it on paper, but probably so, yeah. Everybody sort of went into the tank at the same time--

No. I have some disquieting news for you, which is really not relevant to what we're taping. I don't even know if you want it on tape because it's not important, but let me tell you, during the days that a whole lot of us were hung up, many of the other guys stayed away from it and they did very well and they stayed in town and got into
the studios and did great. Now, the people that were hung are coming out of it; these guys, at this late date are going into it. How do you like that?
I guess that belongs on tape. I guess I'm not sure who you're talking about--I wouldn't ask for names--
I wouldn't give you names.
I'm not sure I understand the pattern.
It's what happens. They've been into it for about ten years now.
To the dumb dope, like heroin?
That's right.
Isn't that strange? That's a whole pattern that I'm not aware of. Am I the only one who has missed this?
No; I think it's known. In New York it's known.
What's going to happen to them?
I have no idea.
I would assume they're successful.
They're not going to be secure for too long, you can be sure of that.
They don't have to feel at this point--
My buddy emptied three of his bank accounts, and one of his businesses. He's still solvent, but he won't be too long.
Is he still playing?
Yeah.
